vulnerabilities.description: Mozilla Firefox Brotli Library Decompression Buffer Overflow
vulnerabilities.detail:
Mozilla Firefox contains a pointer underflow condition in the Brotli library. The issue is triggered as user-supplied input is not properly validated when the library is performing decompression. This may allow a context-dependent attacker to cause a buffer overflow, potentially allowing the execution of arbitrary code.
Due to the vague information available, it is unclear if this only affects Mozilla's implementation of the brotli library or also upstream.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: It has been reported that this has been fixed. Please refer to the product listing for upgraded versions that address this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: Due to the vague information available, it is unclear if this only affects Mozilla's implementation of the brotli library or also upstream.

vulnerabilities.description: Brotli Decoder One-shot Decompression Input Chunk Handling Integer Overflow Buffer Overflow DoS
vulnerabilities.detail:
Brotli contains an integer overflow condition in the decoder that is triggered as large input chunks are not properly handled in one-shot decompression requests. This may allow a context-dependent attacker to cause a buffer overflow, resulting in a denial of service.
Note: Library/framework vulnerability. This code is used in a wide variety of software, and the issue may manifest in a number of different ways. Depending on the implementation, it will vary if this vulnerability requires local or remote access. This issue may not be considered a valid vulnerability for most client applications, but just a stability bug or similar.

Exploitation is possible with input chunks that are larger than 2GiB.

Please note that while the impact of this issue is currently described as crash only, it could theoretically be more severe. However, it has not been demonstrated at this time.
vulnerabilities.recommendation:
It has been reported that this has been fixed. Please refer to the product listing for upgraded versions that address this vulnerability. It is also possible to temporarily mitigate this issue by implementing the following workaround: use the "streaming" API and impose chunk size limits.

While the issue is fixed in version 1.0.8, the vendor recommends to upgrade to version 1.0.9.

vulnerabilities.description: Eclipse Jetty jetty-util Path Traversal Unspecified Issue
vulnerabilities.detail:
Jetty contains a flaw in jetty-utils that allows traversing outside of a restricted path. The issue is due to the application not properly sanitizing input, specifically path traversal style attacks (e.g. '../') supplied via unspecified parameters. This may allow an attacker to have an unspecified impact. No further details have been provided.
Due to the lack of details, this issue can't be matched to an existing entry and may present a duplicate of an already known vulnerability.

This issue is reported in Talend Components, where the affected artifact is blocked. Based on the group ID of the excluded artifact ("org.mortbay.jetty/jetty-util"), the issue affects only older versions.
vulnerabilities.recommendation:
We are not currently aware of a solution for this vulnerability.

This issue is addressed in Talend Components by excluding the affected component.

vulnerabilities.description: ForgeRock OpenAM /openam_sp/UI/Login goto Parameter Open Redirect Weakness
vulnerabilities.detail:
ForgeRock OpenAM contains a flaw that allows a cross-site redirection attack. This flaw exists because the application does not validate the 'goto' parameter upon submission to the /openam_sp/UI/Login script. This could allow a context-dependent attacker to create a specially crafted link that, if followed, would redirect a victim from the intended legitimate web site to an arbitrary web site of the attacker's choosing.

Such attacks are useful as the crafted URL initially appears to be a web page of a trusted site. This could be leveraged to direct an unsuspecting user to a web page containing attacks that target client-side software such as a web browser or document rendering programs, as well as phishing attacks that mimic the legitimate site but send user-supplied information to the attacker.
The vendor says the 'goto' parameter is impacted while the researcher says the 'gotoOnFail' parameter is also impacted.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: It has been reported that this has been fixed. Please refer to the product listing for upgraded versions that address this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: The vendor says the 'goto' parameter is impacted while the researcher says the 'gotoOnFail' parameter is also impacted.

While the issue is referred to as 'unspecified', there is sufficient information for a casual attacker to quickly determine the details required to exploit this issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: It has been reported that this has been fixed. Please refer to the product listing for upgraded versions that address this vulnerability.
